common_name: Chocolate Cherry Tomato (Brownish-Red Heirloom Cherry Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost at 70–80°F and transplant into rich, well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger has passed; stake or cage firmly, since Chocolate Cherry is a vigorous, sprawling indeterminate producer.

directions: Start seed indoors 6–8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into rich, deeply prepared, well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger has passed, staking or caging plants firmly to support their vigorous, indeterminate vines. Chocolate Cherry is an heirloom cherry tomato bearing clusters of round, one-inch fruit in an unusual dusky brownish-red color reminiscent of the larger Cherokee Purple, carrying the same rich, complex, sweet-and-smoky flavor in a bite-sized package rather than a full beefsteak-size fruit. Its productive, long-season vines yield heavily from midsummer through frost, making it a favorite for snacking, salads, and roasting where its deep color and complex flavor stand out from ordinary red cherry tomatoes. Harvest when fruits soften slightly and the color deepens fully, as the dusky skin tone makes visual ripeness cues subtler than on standard red tomatoes.
sources: Seed Savers Exchange — heirloom tomato variety notes

common_name: Sweet 100 Tomato (Classic Prolific Hybrid Cherry Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost at 70–80°F and transplant into rich, well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger has passed; Sweet 100 is an exceptionally vigorous indeterminate hybrid and needs a tall, sturdy cage or trellis to support its long, heavily fruiting vines.

directions: Start seed indoors 6–8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into rich, deeply prepared, well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger has passed, providing a tall, sturdy cage or trellis for the vigorous, sprawling vines. Sweet 100 is a classic F1 hybrid cherry tomato introduced in the 1980s, prized for producing extraordinarily long clusters of small, intensely sweet, bright red fruit in such abundance that a single healthy plant can yield hundreds of tomatoes over the season, giving the variety its name. Its exceptional sweetness, disease tolerance, and reliable heavy production made it one of the most widely grown cherry tomatoes for home gardens and remains a benchmark variety against which many newer cherry tomato hybrids are compared. Harvest continuously as fruit ripens to encourage ongoing production, since the plant sets new clusters rapidly throughout a long summer season.
sources: Cornell University Vegetable Varieties for Gardeners database

common_name: Bonnie Best Tomato (Early 1900s Heirloom Slicing Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost at 70–80°F and transplant into rich, well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger has passed; stake or cage as an indeterminate variety that continues producing over a long season.

directions: Start seed indoors 6–8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into rich, deeply prepared, well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger has passed. Introduced around 1908 and long a staple of American home and market gardens, Bonnie Best produces smooth, deep red, medium-sized fruit with excellent classic tomato flavor and good production over a long season, having served for decades as a standard against which other tomato varieties were measured before modern hybrids became dominant. Its old-fashioned, well-balanced sweet-tart flavor and reliable performance make it a satisfying choice for gardeners seeking a historically significant slicing tomato with genuine heirloom character rather than a specialty color or shape. Harvest when fruit is fully red and yields to gentle pressure, and pick regularly to keep the vigorous vines producing.

common_name: Tommy Toe Tomato (Australian Heirloom Salad Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost at 70–80°F and transplant into rich, well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger has passed; stake or cage firmly, since Tommy Toe is a vigorous, heavy-yielding indeterminate variety.

directions: Start seed indoors 6–8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into rich, deeply prepared, well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger has passed, staking or caging plants firmly to support the vigorous vines. Tommy Toe is a beloved Australian heirloom producing an abundance of round, golf-ball-sized fruit larger than a typical cherry tomato but smaller than a standard slicer, with rich, well-balanced, classic tomato flavor that many gardeners rate above modern cherry hybrids for taste. Its heavy, sustained production over a long season and good disease tolerance have made it a favorite for fresh eating, salads, and snacking straight off the vine, occupying a useful middle ground in size between cherry and full-sized tomatoes. Harvest regularly as fruit ripens to keep the prolific vines setting new fruit throughout the summer.
sources: Seed Savers Exchange — heirloom tomato variety notes
